questions.stem: If the supplier ___ the order today, we will receive it on Friday.

why_wrong: B : pas de « would » dans la proposition en « if » (type 1).
C : le prétérit relève du type 2, incompatible avec « will receive ».
D : pas de « will » dans la proposition en « if ».
fr.example: If it rains, we will stay.

why_wrong: B: no 'would' in the 'if' clause (type 1).
C: the past tense is type 2, incompatible with 'will receive'.
D: no 'will' in the 'if' clause.
en.example: If it rains, we will stay.

questions.stem: If I ___ more time, I would attend the seminar.

why_wrong: A : pas de futur dans la proposition en « if ».
C : type 1, incompatible avec « would ».
D : pas de « would » dans la proposition en « if ».
fr.example: If I were you, I would wait.

en.rule: Type 2: If + simple past, would + verb.
why_wrong: A: no future in the 'if' clause.
C: type 1, incompatible with 'would'.
D: no 'would' in the 'if' clause.
en.example: If I were you, I would wait.

questions.stem: If we ___ the deadline, we would have lost the contract.

fr.rule: Type 3 : If + plus-que-parfait, would have + participe passé.
why_wrong: B : présent, incompatible avec « would have lost ».
C : prétérit simple : il faut le plus-que-parfait (type 3).
D : pas de « would » dans la proposition en « if ».
fr.example: If I had known, I would have called.

en.rule: Type 3: If + past perfect, would have + past participle.
why_wrong: B: present, incompatible with 'would have lost'.
C: simple past: the past perfect is required (type 3).
D: no 'would' in the 'if' clause.
en.example: If I had known, I would have called.

questions.stem: ___ you need further assistance, please contact our help desk.

fr.rule: Should + sujet = If you should (inversion formelle).
why_wrong: A : exprime une obligation.
C : n'est pas l'inversion conditionnelle courante ici.
D : n'a pas ce sens d'inversion conditionnelle.
fr.example: Should you have questions, call me.

en.rule: Should + subject = If you should (formal inversion).
why_wrong: A: expresses obligation.
C: is not the usual conditional inversion here.
D: does not have this conditional inversion meaning.
en.example: Should you have questions, call me.

questions.stem: We will begin the project ___ the client approves the budget.

fr.rule: As long as = à condition que (suivi du présent).
why_wrong: A : exprime l'opposition.
B : exprime l'opposition.
D : le sens serait inversé (sauf si le client approuve).
fr.example: Go as long as you are careful.

en.rule: As long as = provided that (followed by the present).
why_wrong: A: expresses contrast.
B: expresses contrast.
D: the meaning would be reversed (unless the client approves).
en.example: Go as long as you are careful.
